observations.title: Mayon volcano (Philippines)
observations.description: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported ongoing ash emissions and unrest at Mayon during 17-23 September. The seismic network recorded 7-23 daily volcanic earthquakes; one tremor (1-4 minutes long) was recorded on both 18 and 19 September, and one rockfall was detected on both 18 and 20 September. Sulfur dioxide emissions generally averaged 310-1,600 tonnes per day. Daily emissions rose 300-1,000 m above the crater and drifted in different directions. Minor Strombolian activity was observed on 18 September. That same day two visible ash plumes lasted 35 and 46 seconds; the emission at 0844 rose 300 m above the summit and drifted NNE. Three ash emissions, each lasting 1-2 minutes, were recorded on 19 September; one at 1653 with a gray appearance rose 600 m above the summit and drifted NE. A one-minute ash emission occurred on 21 September. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a 0-5 scale) and the public was reminded to stay away from the 6-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ). PHIVOLCS recommended that civil aviation authorities advise pilots to avoid flying close to the summit. Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)
